record.paper_title: Some results and open problems in research on low dimensional organic conductors
record.original_question: Do the phase-diagram results obtained for the one-dimensional extended Hubbard model with on-site interaction U, nearest-neighbor interaction V, and pair-hopping interaction W actually apply to organic conductors such as the Bechgaard salts? The paper reports that this continuum-limit field-theory calculation yields a rich phase diagram containing superconducting, metallic, and four insulating phases, and that the resulting diagrams resemble experimental organic-conductor phase diagrams. The unresolved question is whether that resemblance reflects genuine applicability to real organic conductors despite the omission of crystal-lattice effects.

evidence.quote: It was obtained that this model has a rich phase diagram, which contains a superconducting phase, a metallic phase and four different insulating phases.

The applicability of the results of this work to the organic conductors has not been discussed so far, but it should be noted that the phase diagrams presented in this paper bear strong resemblance to experimental results on the organic conductors.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the one-dimensional extended Hubbard Hamiltonian on a chain of sites $\{i\}$ with spin-1/2 fermion operators $c_{i,\sigma}^\dagger, c_{i,\sigma}$ and number operators $n_{i,\sigma}=c_{i,\sigma}^\dagger c_{i,\sigma}$, $n_i = n_{i,\uparrow}+n_{i,\downarrow}$:
$$
H = -t\sum_{i,\sigma}(c_{i,\sigma}^\dagger c_{i+1,\sigma}+\text{h.c.}) + U\sum_i n_{i,\uparrow}n_{i,\downarrow} + V\sum_i n_i n_{i+1} + W\sum_i \big(c_{i,\uparrow}^\dagger c_{i,\downarrow}^\dagger c_{i+1,\downarrow}c_{i+1,\uparrow}+\text{h.c.}\big),
$$
where $U$ is the on-site interaction, $V$ the nearest-neighbor density-density interaction, and $W$ the pair-hopping (singlet-pair tunneling) amplitude. A continuum-limit bosonization/field-theory analysis of this model at (or near) quarter or half filling yields a phase diagram in the $(U,V,W)$ parameter space containing a superconducting phase, a metallic (Luttinger-liquid) phase, and four distinct insulating phases (charge-density-wave, spin-density-wave, bond-order-wave, and singlet-pairing insulator types).

The question is: do the phase-diagram features predicted by this purely one-dimensional continuum model — which neglects three-dimensional crystal-lattice structure, inter-chain coupling, and lattice-phonon effects — actually describe the experimentally observed phase diagrams of quasi-one-dimensional organic conductors of the Bechgaard-salt family $(\mathrm{TMTSF})_2 X$ and $(\mathrm{TMTTF})_2 X$? Equivalently, is the qualitative resemblance between the model's $(U,V,W)$ phase diagram and the empirical pressure–temperature phase diagrams of these compounds a consequence of a genuine applicability of the model, or an accidental similarity that fails once realistic crystal-lattice effects are restored?
artifact.status_search_result: The applicability of the one-dimensional extended Hubbard model with on-site, nearest-neighbor, and pair-hopping interactions to real Bechgaard salts remains a debated, open question. Subsequent literature continues to study extensions (including inter-chain coupling, dimerization, and electron-phonon effects), but no definitive consensus has been established that the simple 1D $U$–$V$–$W$ phase diagram faithfully represents the experimental phase diagram of organic conductors.

status_evidence.claim: The question of applicability to real organic conductors is explicitly listed as unresolved.
